business_scope.primary_industry_name: Remote Desktop Access and Unattended Machine Telemetry Software

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Switzerland – Federal/Cantonal dual registry system (registered seat in canton of incorporation)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Romano-Germanic tradition with strong federal statutory framework and cantonal notarial competence)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: EFTA Convention (1960, as consolidated) and EFTA Free Trade Agreements network
Switzerland–EU Bilateral Agreements I (1999, sectoral market access)
Switzerland–United States DTA (1951 as amended) and residual 1850 Treaty of Friendship, Commerce and Consular Rights

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Swiss Code of Obligations (SR 220) Arts. 626, 640, 950; Commercial Register Ordinance (HRegV, SR 221.411) Arts. 2–5, 9, 38; Federal Act on Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (AMLA, SR 955.0) Arts. 2–3, 6–9; FINMA Anti-Money Laundering Ordinance (AMLO-FINMA, SR 955.022) Arts. 15–20; Federal Act on the Transparency of Legal Entities and the Identification of Beneficial Owners (TJPG, SR 221.421, in force 1 November 2023) introducing CO Arts. 927i–927j and Civil Code Arts. 52a–52b; Embargo Act (SR 946.231) and SECO sanctions ordinances; Hague Apostille Convention (SR 211.213.2).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity card of each shareholder and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent passport/ID authority of country of nationality (foreign) or Swiss cantonal authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via issuing state's competent authority (for foreign public documents); Swiss-issued documents apostilled by Cantonal Chancery; photographic copy additionally certified by Swiss notary public

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified extract from foreign commercial register (if corporate shareholder or intermediate holding entity)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company register / commercial registrar of country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the issuing state; Swiss domestic shareholders provide a current excerpt from the Swiss Commercial Register (no apostille required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill, bank statement, or municipal residence certificate) of each UBO and director
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider / recognized financial institution / municipal registry (Einwohnerkontrolle)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for municipal public certificates; notarization of signatory authority for private documents (apostille not required under Hague Convention for private instruments)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds confirmation from deposit-taking institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization of bank signatory authority only (private document; no apostille required); Swiss notarial certification of signature

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for incorporation formalities and registered-office-managed statutory filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Internal Swiss notarial act (no apostille or consular legalization required for domestic notarial deeds)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based CDD under AMLA Art. 3: identify all natural-person beneficial owners at the ≥25% capital or voting-rights threshold; screen against SECO consolidated sanctions lists (UN Security Council and EU regimes adopted by Switzerland), Swiss anti-terrorism financing ordinances under the Embargo Act, and OFAC SDN list for any USD payment rails; Swiss domestic PEP definition is extended beyond FATF and includes all holders of senior public functions at federal, cantonal, and communal levels; initial PEP screening at onboarding, annual re-screening, and continuous monitoring required under AMLO-FINMA Arts. 15–20; findings must be documented in the client due diligence file retained for ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Zefix – Central Business Name Index (www.zefix.ch), operated by the Federal Commercial Register Office (EHRA/FBOA), in conjunction with the competent Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt); preliminary name check (Voranmeldung) must be filed with the cantonal office for the intended registered seat; publication thereafter in the Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name (Firma) may be formulated in German, French, Italian, or Romansh, or any combination thereof; foreign-language additions are permissible only if written in Latin script and not misleading; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin script in the commercial register; the name must contain 'Aktiengesellschaft' or the abbreviation 'AG' and must accurately reflect the company's business scope without creating material misrepresentation (Art. 950 CO; Arts. 2–5 HRegV).
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: European Union / UNO / Rotes Kreuz / Red Cross
Names of cantons, municipalities, and public-law institutions without prior authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon formal rejection, the applicant may request a written decree (Verfügung) from the Cantonal Commercial Register Office; appeal against that decree lies to the cantonal supervisory or administrative appeal authority within 30 days of service; further appeal is available to the Federal Administrative Court (Bundesverwaltungsgericht), and ultimately to the Federal Supreme Court (Bundesgericht) on legal grounds; the expedited commercial path is to resubmit a revised name incorporating distinguishing elements (geographical, activity, or capitalization descriptors) without formal appeal; name reservations may be extended on application before expiry upon showing of good cause, subject to the two-year statutory maximum under Art. 38 HRegV.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permitted: the registered office (Sitz) must be a real, physically addressable location in the canton of incorporation where statutory records are kept and official service of process can be made (Art. 626 CO); the center of administration (Verwaltungssitz) is presumed to be at the registered office unless the articles of association provide otherwise (Art. 327c CO). For a remote screen-share/IoT software company, the standard market solution is a licensed domiciliation provider (Sitzgesellschaftsdienstleister) offering a genuine Swiss business address, mail handling, and statutory record custody; mail-forwarding-only PO boxes or letterbox addresses are non-compliant. Since the 2023 AMLA reform, domiciliation service providers are themselves subject to AML supervision, raising the compliance quality of accepted virtual-office arrangements.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low: approximately 5–8% annual probability of unannounced verification for a non-regulated, low-risk software issuer without financial intermediary status; verification typically occurs through the licensed domiciliation provider's own AML inspection obligations or upon third-party complaint to the Cantonal Commercial Register Office; FINMA on-site supervision is not applicable absent a financial intermediary license.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal preliminary name clearance (Voranmeldung) and name reservation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Art. 38 HRegV; cantonal fee tariff (typical CHF 50–100)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of Articles of Association (Statuten) before Swiss notary public
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Cantonal notarial tariff based on share capital (market range CHF 500–1,200)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of constitutional documents and UBO forms (German/French/Italian into English or reverse)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (CHF 400–800 per document set)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign UBO identity, address, and corporate registry documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Cantonal Chancery (for Swiss-origin apostilles) or competent authority of the foreign issuing state
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Hague Apostille Convention (SR 211.213.2); CHF 150–300 per document

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Cantonal Commercial Register incorporation registration fee (AG)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Art. 9 HRegV; cantonal fee tariff (typical CHF 600–1,500 depending on share capital)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB) publication of incorporation
UBO register initial drafting, director declarations, and TJPG compliance setup
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Incorporation counsel (law firm or licensed fiduciary)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market fixed fee; CO Arts. 927i–927j and CC Arts. 52a–52b compliance scope

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office with licensed domiciliation and administrative representation provider (annual fee)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Licensed domiciliation service provider (subject to AMLA 2023)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for software/Tech companies (CHF 2,400–4,800 per annum)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: PEP and sanctions screening (SECO, UN, OFAC) and CDD file preparation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: AMLA Art. 3 CDD requirements; market benchmark per UBO (CHF 800–1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarized power of attorney for incorporation formalities and courier/certified copy charges
Legal advisory fixed fee for Stage 1 pre-incorporation due diligence, UBO structure analysis, and board minutes drafting
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Swiss law firm or licensed fiduciary

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Swiss Code of Obligations (Obligationenrecht, OR), Articles 620-763 (Aktienrecht / droit de la société anonyme); supplementary provisions of the Federal Act on Product Liability and the Swiss Merger Act where applicable
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office (Handelsregisteramt / Office du registre du commerce) under the supervisory authority of the Federal Commercial Register Office (Eidgenössisches Amt für das Handelsregister, EAR); electronic filing via the eGRIS platform
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Gründungsurkunde / acte de constitution) together with the Articles of Association (Statuten / statuts), filed in original before the Commercial Register
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum nominal share capital of CHF 100,000 (approximately USD 113,000), of which at least CHF 50,000 (approximately USD 56,500) must be fully paid up in cash at incorporation; the paid-in amount must be deposited in a blocked capital escrow account (Sperrkonto / compte de consignation) at a licensed Swiss bank and is released only after the company is entered in the Commercial Register
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The incorporators hereby resolve: (1) the share capital of CHF 100,000 has been fully subscribed and CHF 50,000 has been paid up and deposited in a blocked capital escrow account; (2) the Articles of Association are adopted and the registered seat of the company is established in Switzerland; (3) the Board of Directors is appointed, namely [Name] as Chairman, [Name] as Member, and a licensed audit firm shall be engaged if statutory thresholds are exceeded; (4) the Board is authorized to open corporate bank accounts, instruct the notary and Commercial Register, and apply for the Swiss UID, VAT, AHV employer, and any required permits; (5) the Chairman jointly with any other Board member holds signature authority and representation power for registration matters.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name Pre-Clearance and Legal Form Pre-Validation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office with coordination through the Swiss Central Name Search Portal (ZEFIX)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a full-text and phonetic name search in ZEFIX to verify that the proposed business name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered name, is not misleading, and includes the legal-form suffix 'AG'. Confirm that the company seat in the chosen canton is permissible and the business purpose clause matches the intended ISIC 6201 remote desktop software activities. Obtain informal pre-validation from the Commercial Register if the name involves non-standard elements.
required_dossiers: Proposed company name with legal-form suffix
Draft Articles of Association (Statuten / statuts)
Statement of intended registered seat
Declared business purpose (software development, remote access, IoT telemetry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried, amend the proposed name and resubmit the pre-validation request; alternatively, request a formal written decision from the Commercial Register and appeal within 30 days to the cantonal supervisory authority or appeal court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Deed of Incorporation and Adoption of Articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Notary Public (Notariat / Office du notaire) authorized in the canton of the registered seat
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and finalize the Articles of Association in German, French, or Italian in accordance with the language of the canton. Present the incorporators before the notary for certification of identity, confirm full subscription of the CHF 100,000 share capital, declare the amount paid in, and execute the public deed of incorporation (öffentliche Beurkundung). The notary must certify the deed and transmit it to the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or identity card of each incorporator and director
Final Articles of Association signed by all incorporators
Declaration of share subscription and capital payment
Residence/domicile documentation of each director (residence requirement for at least one director resident in Switzerland)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies deficiencies in the articles or capital declaration, prepare a corrective supplementary deed or re-execute the notarization; any statutory defects may be cured before submission to the Commercial Register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of Blocked Capital Escrow Account and Deposit of Paid-Up Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Swiss Bank (e.g., UBS, Credit Suisse, Zürcher Kantonalbank, Zuger Kantonalbank, or other FINMA-supervised bank)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked capital account (Sperrkonto / compte de consignation) in the company's future name, transfer CHF 50,000 as the minimum statutory paid-up capital, and instruct the bank to issue a written capital payment confirmation (Bestätigung der Kapitalzahlung / confirmation de versement). The bank holds the funds in escrow and will only release them to the company upon presentation of the Commercial Register entry certificate.
required_dossiers: Approved name confirmation from ZEFIX or Commercial Register
Draft Articles of Association
Powers of attorney for account signatories
Identification documents of the incorporators and beneficial owners
Client due diligence form under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (AMLA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank queries the application due to AML or KYC concerns, provide additional source-of-funds documentation or engage a licensed fiduciary to support the file; select an alternative FINMA-regulated bank if the initial bank declines the account without cure.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Registration with the Commercial Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cantonal Commercial Register Office via the eGRIS electronic filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for entry of the Aktiengesellschaft in the Commercial Register using the official eGRIS platform or the cantonal registry's electronic channel. Attach the notarized deed of incorporation, the signed Articles of Association, the bank capital payment confirmation, signed specimen signature cards, and the statutory declarations. The company acquires legal personality upon the date of entry in the Commercial Register.
required_dossiers: Notarized deed of incorporation (Gründungsurkunde / acte de constitution)
Articles of Association (Statuten / statuts)
Blocked capital account bank confirmation
Specimen signature cards of the Board of Directors and authorized signatories
Declaration confirming compliance with the qualified residence requirement (at least one director resident in Switzerland)
Consent of auditors if audited status applies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Register issues a defect notice or amendment order, cure the stated deficiency within the statutory cure period, usually 30 days from notification, by submitting corrected documents or an explanatory memo; appeal an unfavorable rejection to the cantonal Commercial Register supervisory commission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Registration, UID Allocation, and SHAB Publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Federal Commercial Register Office and Swiss Official Gazette of Commerce (SHAB); Swiss Federal Statistical Office for the UID
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon entry of the company, obtain the official excerpt from the Commercial Register (Handelsregisterauszug / extrait du registre du commerce). The Swiss Business Identification Number (UID) is automatically assigned and communicated. The registry submits the registration notice to SHAB for its mandatory official publication. The bank release of the blocked capital account is then authorized by presentation of the entry confirmation.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register entry confirmation
Issued UID number
Final name and seat as recorded in the registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the SHAB publication contains data errors, file a request for rectification with the Commercial Register Office; incorrect UID data should be corrected through the UID register online portal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Registration Ancillary Obligations: VAT, AHV Employer, and Administrative Permits
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV / FTA), cantonal tax administration, and cantonal equalization/compensation office (Ausgleichskasse / caisse de compensation)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register for VAT if annual taxable turnover is expected to exceed CHF 250,000 or voluntarily at a lower threshold for input VAT recovery. Register as an employer with the cantonal compensation office for AHV, IV, EO, ALV, and BVG social insurance contributions. Confirm that no industrial or operating permit is required for ISIC 6201 software activities, and file any municipal or cantonal administrative notices as required for office-based operations.
required_dossiers: Commercial Register excerpt and UID
VAT registration form as applicable
AHV employer registration form
Bank details for social contributions
Lease agreement or registered office consent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax or AHV authorities impose late-filing penalties, submit a written rescision request demonstrating timely underlying registration efforts and pay any assessed contribution; engage a Swiss fiduciary to manage retroactive registrations and penalty waivers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO) and Cantonal Office for Economic Affairs — no industrial license applicable to ISIC 6201 computer programming, remote desktop access, or unattended machine telemetry software activities
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — software publishing and ICT services are not classified as license-requiring activities under the Swiss Federal Act on Economic Activities or cantonal industrial statutes; a general municipal business registration may apply only for physical office premises

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN / BAFU / OFEV) acting through cantonal environmental protection authorities
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based and cloud-delivered software service; no project listed under Annex 1 of the Swiss Environmental Impact Assessment Ordinance (UVPV / OEIA) applies, and therefore no EIA report or environmental registration is required
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No point-source industrial discharges or VOC emissions generated by software operations; compliance obligations are limited to sanitary wastewater from office premises under the Waters Protection Act (GSchG) and the Waters Protection Ordinance (GSchV), municipal solid waste disposal under the Technical Ordinance on Waste (VVEA), and low-voltage/electromagnetic compliance for office IT equipment under applicable Swiss electrical safety standards

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the cantonal fire prevention authority (Feuerpolizei / police du feu) confirming occupancy load, escape routes, extinguishing equipment, and compliance with Swiss fire protection norms (VKF/AEAI); structural load inspection for office premises is required only if alterations affect statics; occupational health and safety clearance under SECO and Suva guidelines covering workplace ergonomics, IT equipment workstations, electrical installations, and first-aid provisions; no special hazardous-installation clearance applies to pure software activities

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (Eidgenössische Steuerverwaltung ESTV / Administration fédérale des contributions AFC / Amministrazione federale delle contribuzioni AFC), official portal www.estv.admin.ch; UID registry and commercial register portal www.zefix.ch; cantonal tax administrations impose and administer cantonal/communal corporate income tax and capital tax.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Swiss or foreign entity engaged in taxable activities in Switzerland must obtain a Swiss VAT registration number (MWST-Nr / TVA-Nr / IVA-Nr) by filing the VAT registration form with ESTV before the start of taxable activity. The business identification number (Unternehmens-Identifikationsnummer UID / numéro IDE / numero IDI) is issued automatically upon entry in the Swiss Commercial Register (Zefix) and serves as the common tax number for federal, cantonal, and municipal tax purposes. A non-resident company without a Swiss registered office but with Swiss-source turnover above CHF 100,000 must use the simplified foreign-supplier registration scheme, submitting ESTV Form 034 and, where requested, appointing or arranging a fiscal representative. The cantonal tax number is allocated by the cantonal tax office of the registered seat or permanent establishment once the first tax filing is accepted.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election is available under Swiss law; legal form determines tax classification (Aktiengesellschaft is a taxable entity). Relevant statutory elections include: (i) Swiss VAT group election (Art. 11 of the Swiss VAT Act), allowing a fiscal unity to file as one taxpayer; (ii) participation deduction election for qualifying dividends and capital gains (Art. 69 and Art. 70 of the Federal Direct Tax Act); (iii) patent box election for qualifying IP income (reduced taxation of up to 90% of such income, Art. 24b para. 2 of the Federal Direct Tax Act); (iv) notional interest deduction on excess equity as an optional cantonal measure after the Swiss Tax Reform 17; (v) election to apply simplified export zero-rating documentation for small consignments; and (vi) election for the disclosure of hidden reserves in a tax-neutral restructuring under Art. 61 of the Federal Direct Tax Act. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are not elective: Swiss law imposes mandatory anti-abuse limitation on deduction denial for cross-border hybrid arrangements consistent with OECD BEPS Action 2.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Swiss Value Added Tax (Mehrwertsteuer / Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Federal Act of 12 June 2009 on Value Added Tax (VATA).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CHF 100,000 annual world-wide turnover from taxable supplies (Art. 10 VATA), after deducting exempt supplies; foreign suppliers performing supplies in Switzerland exceeding CHF 100,000 Swiss-source turnover must register irrespective of any permanent establishment; foreign suppliers of electronic services to Swiss private customers are liable to register regardless of the threshold using the simplified OSS-like procedure, unless turnover is below CHF 100,000 and they apply the small-business exemption.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Switzerland does not operate a real-time fiscal clearance system and does not require digital stamping or government pre-clearance of invoices. Swiss VAT law recognizes paper and electronic invoices equally. For domestic B2B invoicing, the financial industry standard is the Swiss QR-bill and the SIX eBill platform (VeDA/SIX); PEPPOL BIS UBL-based e-invoicing is increasingly accepted for public procurement and large commercial counterparties. The ESTV provides an online e-services portal for VAT returns, XML-based periodic files, and structured electronic registration. There is no mandatory API-based continuous transaction control; eBill or QR-bill interchange uses proprietary bank APIs and contractual PEPPOL sample by mutual agreement.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods exports qualify for 0% Swiss VAT where the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of Switzerland to a foreign destination and are intended for permanent export or to be processed abroad (Art. 23 VATA). Services qualify for zero-rating when the place of supply is outside Switzerland, including remote software services, screen-sharing and IoT telemetry supplied to a recipient with an establishment abroad, provided the effective benefit and usage occur outside Switzerland (Art. 18 para. 2 lit. b VATA). For ISIC 6201 remote desktop software, zero-rating is available where the foreign recipient is a business or non-Swiss private person resident abroad and the supply consists of a digital service the place of which is determined by the customer's residence or establishment, not by the server location.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Swiss Customs Export Declaration (e-dec) confirming the physical exit of exported goods or the technical export declaration number for service-related documentation
Bill of Lading / CMB / CMR or Air Waybill evidencing transport from the Swiss customs territory to the foreign destination
Inward Remittance Certificate showing receipt of the export consideration in foreign currency or through a Swiss bank account in the name of the exporter
Commercial invoice, contract, and (where applicable) Swiss export zero-rating supporting statement identifying the foreign recipient, ISIC 6201 scope description, and the applicable zero-rate basis
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ESTV may retrospectively assess VAT on goods or services claimed as zero-rated exports if the exporter fails to deliver a complete export evidence bundle within the statutory inspection period. The regular limitation period for VAT assessments is ten years. In case of fraudulent substantiation such as fictitious exports, false e-dec data, or forged inbound remittance certificates, the VAT is clawed back together with default interest (currently 4.5% per annum) and may attract an administrative fine of up to three times the tax evaded (Art. 39 VATA). Deliberate tax evasion can additionally incur criminal fines, and customs offences for false export declarations are sanctioned separately with confiscation and penalties. For remote software and digital services, ESTV scrutinizes the place-of-establishment of the recipient and any evidence of use/benefit in Switzerland; a mismatch between contract counterparty, payment origin, and IP addresses may trigger full reassessment.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Swiss National Bank (SNB) / Eidgenössische Finanzmarktaufsicht FINMA (regulatory authority for banks and financial intermediaries)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Swiss franc is fully convertible with no foreign-exchange control restrictions on current or capital account transactions. Profit remittance hurdles are limited to Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) at 35% on dividends, which may be reduced or refunded under an applicable tax treaty or through the Swiss participation relief regime. No exchange-control approval is required for dividend distributions, loan repayments, or capital repatriation, but corporate substance, transfer-pricing documentation, and the absence of abusive tax structuring must be demonstrated to preserve treaty access.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Switzerland imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation timeline, or minimum conversion ratio for export proceeds. Exporters may lawfully retain foreign currency in Swiss or offshore bank accounts, convert freely at market rates, and use such funds for operational or investment purposes without SNB authorization.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (CHF/EUR/USD); Capital Escrow Account available for share capital deposit
Commercial Current Account and Capital Escrow Account for resident and non-resident owned AGs
Operational Corporate Account with payment and liquidity management facilities

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-to-moderate for core treasury clearing. Switzerland is not in the EEA, so foreign electronic money institutions cannot passport into Switzerland; a third-country EMI requires either a FINMA banking licence or a licensed Swiss bank partnership to issue local IBANs and process SIC/SEPA payments. EMIs are viable only as complementary merchant collection gateways (e.g., Stripe, Paddle) and may not serve as the primary regulated clearing rail for inbound capital or large trade disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most Tier-1 Swiss banks require at least one in-person meeting with the ultimate beneficial owner, directors, and a responsible signatory during onboarding. Remote video-identification is accepted by some banks under FINMA-compliant procedures, but initial account opening for a newly incorporated AG with non-resident shareholders is more likely to require physical appearance at the bank's office or an official representative. Documentation must be certified as true copies by a notary public or Swiss consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner with residence in a FATF-high-risk or monitored jurisdiction
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Passport copy with apostille, board resolution, corporate excerpt (Handelsregisterauszug), proof of economic activity, source-of-wealth statement, bank reference letter, and a written explanation of the commercial nexus to Switzerland.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial paid-in share capital
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Personal and corporate bank statements showing the origin of funds, signed share subscription and payment receipts, audited or certified financial statements, tax returns, and legal agreements supporting the transfer of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Remote-only software business selling low-ticket recurring subscriptions via third-party payment platforms without local substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Service agreements, annual recurring revenue report, payment platform settlement statements, customer invoices, software usage telemetry, evidence of Swiss operational substance (lease, payroll, board minutes), and an independent AML risk assessment classifying the business as low-risk standard.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid cross-border cash flows with no procurement or trade documentation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Invoices, purchase orders, delivery or service performance logs, transport and customs documentation, SWIFT MT103 reference details, and an internal treasury policy explaining counterparty risk and payment justification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct CHF or EUR transfers from the beneficial owner's account to the Swiss AG's capital escrow account. The payment must reference 'Share Capital Contribution' and include a bank reference identifying the purpose code for direct investment or capital contribution. No SNB exchange-control approval is required, but the receiving Swiss bank must obtain source-of-funds evidence and may require beneficiary attestation. For amounts above CHF 50,000, Swiss AML and international reporting standards trigger standard enhanced screening; cross-border payments above applicable thresholds may also need inclusion in the Swiss National Bank balance-of-payments reporting survey if the bank reports it on behalf of the enterprise. Ensure the beneficiary legal name, address, and IBAN exactly match the corporate register entry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Prime clearing rails are SWIFT MT103 for international supplier payments, SWIFT MT202 COV for bank-to-bank settlement transfers, SEPA Instant for EUR-denominated payments within Europe, and SIC (Swiss Interbank Clearing) for domestic CHF payments. Trade settlements may be effected via irrevocable documentary letters of credit (UCP 600) using SWIFT MT700 issuance and MT710 amendment, with SWIFT MT754 reimbursement for commercial LC settlement. For digital subscription software services, the cash-in rails are Stripe and Paddle, which settle via their respective acquiring banks into the Swiss operational account; cash-outs to international contractors are executed via MT103 with descriptive purpose codes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Over-the-Counter FX forwards in CHF/EUR/USD
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for long-term balance-sheet hedging
Vanilla FX options (call and put) on major freely convertible currencies
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currency exposure where local deliverability is restricted

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual federal and cantonal corporate income tax declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cantonal tax administration with Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV) coordination
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within 6 months after fiscal year-end (varies by canton; extension available)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing interest of 5% per annum; defaulted tax assessment; fines up to CHF 10,000 for willful non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual capital tax return (included in cantonal/municipal tax declaration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as annual tax declaration; no separate filing deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest on unpaid capital tax and enforceable collection proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT return (if annual settlement option elected; otherwise quarterly/semestrial)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV), VAT Division
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: If annual filing: within 60 days after close of tax period (year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default interest of 5% per annum; serious violations prosecuted under VAT law with fines up to CHF 10,000 or more

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register notification of any changes in directors, share capital and bye-laws (event-driven, not calendrical)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days of occurrence of registrable change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Official penalty of up to CHF 5,000 for late registration; failure to register may trigger removal from the commercial register in extreme cases

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Ordinary audit (full independent audit) is mandatory if any two of the following three criteria are exceeded in two consecutive years: total assets above CHF 20 million, annual turnover above CHF 40 million, average annual employment above 250 full-time equivalents. A limited audit is required for smaller companies unless an opting-out resolution is passed (permitted for companies with fewer than 10 full-time employees and annual turnover below CHF 2 million).
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Annual financial statements must comply with Swiss Code of Obligations (Swiss GAAP CO); IFRS is permissible for consolidated accounts of listed or economically significant entities; Swiss GAAP FER is accepted for some regulated sectors.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Swiss law does not prescribe an annual UBO confirmation filing to the federal register; however, under the new Swiss Federal Act on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RoBO), companies are obliged to record the beneficial owner(s) of their shareholding and to make such data available to competent authorities upon request. Any change in shareholders or capital is reported to the Commercial Register within 14 days, and the share register must be updated continuously.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Switzerland imposes direct federal tax (DFT) at 8.5% of net profit after federal tax, equivalent to an effective 7.83% of pre-tax profit; combined federal, cantonal and communal effective corporate income tax rate in the canton of Zug (2024) is approximately 11.9% on pre-tax profit; the statutory combined range across Swiss cantons is approximately 11.9% to 21.0%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Patent/IP Box under the Swiss TRAF tax reform (SR 642.1): 90% of qualifying net IP income from patents and comparable IP rights is exempt at both federal and cantonal level, subject to an overall cap limiting the combined patent box and R&D super-deduction relief to 50% of taxable profit; R&D Super-Deduction: additional deductible amount of up to 50% of eligible Swiss R&D personnel and related costs, raising the total deduction to up to 150% of the qualifying cost base (implemented in Zug); Participation Relief (Art. 70 DBG): 100% exemption of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from participations of >=10% held for at least one year; Notional Interest Deduction (NID) on excess safety equity is optional by canton and not currently applied in Zug; traditional cantonal holding/domicile company regimes were abolished as of 1 January 2020.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Combined cantonal and federal corporate income tax return Form ZG 201 (Formulaire B / personnes morales) for Aktiengesellschaften, filed electronically through the canton Zug online tax portal (e-Tax Zug / SwissTax DEBIS suite) using the official Swiss business identifier (UID / CHE-number); the federal profit tax return (EstV 201) and the canton Zug tax return are consolidated in a single filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual, once per statutory business year; additional short-period returns are required only upon liquidation, relocation of seat, change of accounting date, or taxable restructuring.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Statutory filing deadline is within six months after the end of the business year (Art. 126 DBG; §§ 97-98 of the Zug Tax Act); for a 31 December year-end, the return is due by 30 June of the following year; extension of generally up to three months may be granted upon written application to the Zug tax administration, and further professional extensions are commonly allowed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company legal name, UID/CHE registration number, registered seat, purpose, board members, authorised representatives, fiscal year and accounting currency.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and non-resident directors do not sign the return unless individually required; the AG must be represented by a person authorised under Art. 127 DBG, being a Swiss resident director or a duly appointed Swiss tax agent with power of attorney, both of whom are personally identifiable in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statutory balance sheet per Art. 958-963 OR: total assets, liquid funds, trade receivables from Stripe/Paddle settlement accounts, deferred revenue, share capital (minimum CHF 100,000, of which at least CHF 50,000 paid-in), statutory capital reserves, free reserves, and accumulated profit/loss.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident group parent must ensure the Swiss entity maintains full books and records in Switzerland; a Swiss GAAP FER or OR-compliant annual report is required; tax balance sheet must be submitted even when the parent prepares IFRS consolidated statements.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 / Income Statement and Business Revenue
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Detailed profit and loss statement: gross subscription revenue from remote screen share and IoT telemetry software, support fees, cost of sales, personnel costs, third-party cloud hosting, marketing, depreciation and EBITDA-to-net-profit bridge.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Revenue must be recognised ratably over SaaS subscription terms and allocated according to the place of effective use for Swiss tax purposes; revenue collected by Stripe/Paddle as payment facilitators must be fully declared, with merchant fees deducted as allowable business expenses.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation of the commercial net profit to taxable profit: add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., 50% of non-business representation costs, tax-exempt foreign losses, concealed profit distributions, excessive director compensation), and deduction of tax-exempt income (participation dividends).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an AG controlled by a foreign parent, any shareholder loan with above-market interest or unpaid management fees may be reclassified as a constructive dividend subject to 35% withholding tax; transfer pricing adjustments under Art. 58a DBG must be reflected in the tax return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Patent Box, R&D Super-Deduction and Participation Relief
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of qualifying IP income qualifying for the 90% patent box exclusion; additional R&D super-deduction claim; participation relief claims for qualifying dividend income and capital gains with supporting schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-parent entities must substantiate that Swiss-registered IP is developed through Swiss nexus activities; outsourced R&D performed by related foreign companies does not qualify. The combined patent box and R&D deduction is capped at 50% of the taxable profit before such reliefs.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Taxable Profit and Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable profit after adjustments; apportionment between federal and cantonal/communal bases; computation of direct federal tax at 8.5% of post-tax profit, and Zug cantonal/communal tax at the applicable proportional rate and commune factor.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident parent is not itself liable to Swiss income tax on the AG's retained profits; however, the AG must attach certified evidence of foreign tax credits if the parent jurisdiction (e.g., PRC) demands CFC/controlled foreign company inclusion of Swiss profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: procedural fine (Ordnungsbusse) of up to CHF 10,000 (Art. 147 DBG; § 137 Zug Tax Act) plus default interest at approximately 4.5% per annum; failure to respond to formal demand triggers discretionary assessment (Art. 130 DBG) at increased taxable basis. Negligent underdeclaration: penalty of two-thirds of the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); intentional evasion: fine of up to three times the evaded tax; tax fraud with falsified or forged documents (Art. 186 DBG): imprisonment up to three years or a criminal fine. The Federal Tax Administration may order seizure of assets as security for the evaded amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Swiss federal withholding tax (Verrechnungssteuer) is 35% of the gross dividend, withheld by the Swiss resident paying company (the AG) and remitted to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration (ESTV/SIF) within 30 days of distribution (Art. 13, 17 VStG).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The AG must withhold 35% at source notwithstanding the treaty; the beneficial owner applies to the ESTV for a refund of the excess under the Switzerland-China DTA (2013), which reduces the rate to 5% for dividends paid to a company that holds directly at least 10% of the AG's voting capital and is the beneficial owner, and to 10% in all other cases. Protocol: (1) obtain a valid Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the Chinese (or other treaty-resident) tax authority covering the dividend payment year; (2) file the refund claim with the Swiss Federal Tax Administration using Form 110-N/N1 (or the ESTV DTA refund form) through the AG or the paying bank, attaching the TRC, dividend resolution, and proof of payment; (3) submit the claim within three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became due (Art. 23 para. 1 VStG); (4) in appropriate cases the ESTV may authorise an advance reduction ('Entlastungsverfahren') of the withholding rate upon prior written approval, but the regular refund procedure remains the standard route. The AG is jointly liable if it distributes dividends to a shareholder known to be a mere conduit without economic substance.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Swiss law imposes no statutory withholding tax on ordinary intercompany interest or on technical/royalty licence fees; the 35% withholding tax applies only to dividends and to interest on Swiss-issued bonds and money-market paper (subject to the Art. 4 VStG bank exemption). Under the Switzerland-China DTA the maximum source-state rate on interest is 10% and on royalties 10%, but because Switzerland refrains from source taxation, the DTA rates are generally invoked only on the Chinese side for outbound payments from a PRC payer; interest deductibility in Switzerland remains subject to arm's-length conditions and hidden equity distribution rules under Art. 65 DBG.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation (Local File and Master File) is triggered in Switzerland when the consolidated group annual turnover exceeds CHF 80 million for the sale of goods or CHF 20 million for services (Art. 58a DBG, FTA Circular on TP documentation); for a remote screen share and IoT telemetry software entity, the CHF 20 million services threshold applies. Below these thresholds the AG is not exempt from establishing arm's-length pricing; the tax authorities may request documentation and impose penalties up to CHF 10,000 plus interest where the taxpayer fails to substantiate the transaction price. A Swiss safe harbour for low-value-adding intra-group routine services allows a cost-plus mark-up of or an equivalent net margin of approximately 5%, aligning with the OECD simplified approach.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Switzerland has no general Economic Substance Regulation in the style of the UAE or other offshore regimes; however, the AG must demonstrate genuine substance in Switzerland to sustain treaty benefits and domestic participation relief. Substance indicia include a Swiss registered office with physical premises, a Swiss VAT registration where required, a Swiss bank account, payroll and social security contributions for Swiss staff, board meetings and actual management decisions taken in Switzerland, and local development or monitoring of the core IoT software IP. A letterbox or sham company whose management and critical functions are located abroad may be recharacterised under the abuse-of-law doctrine (Art. 21 VStG and Swiss tax jurisprudence), leading to denial of the treaty refund and participation exemption, reallocation of profits to the foreign parent, and back-taxes with penalty. Additionally, groups with consolidated annual revenue of EUR 750 million or more are subject to the Swiss OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax rules (QDMTT and IIR) at 15% effective rate from 2025; the present low-revenue AG is outside that scope.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentional or grossly negligent omission of revenue from Stripe/Paddle settlement reports, undisclosed licence or telemetry service income, inflation of deductible expenses, or suppression of foreign bank accounts and crypto-asset holdings in the Swiss corporate tax return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal penalty of up to three times the evaded tax (Art. 175 DBG); cantonal Zug penalty of up to three times the evaded tax; reduction to two-thirds for negligence; default interest of approximately 4.5% per annum; criminal tax fraud with fraudulent books or documents (Art. 186 DBG) is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years, and the tax debt remains collectible with compulsory enforcement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and managing officers who cause or permit the evasion are jointly and severally liable under Art. 52 DBG for the company's unpaid taxes and under Art. 12 VStG for unremitted withholding tax; the corporate veil may be pierced where funds are diverted; individual criminal convictions can trigger travel bans, asset freezes, extradition requests, and disqualification from holding Swiss board positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to Withhold and Remit 35% Anticipatory Tax
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distribution of a dividend, advance payment, deemed distribution, or shareholder benefit without deducting the 35% Swiss withholding tax, or failure to remit the withheld amount to the Swiss Federal Tax Administration within 30 days.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Collection of the full unremitted 35% withholding tax from the AG plus default interest; administrative fine of up to three times the evaded withholding tax under the VStG; criminal prosecution for wilful non-remittance under Art. 63-65 VStG with imprisonment up to three years or monetary penalty.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members are personally, jointly and severally liable under Art. 12 VStG for the unpaid withholding tax and penalties, regardless of whether the company remains solvent; civil recovery actions may reach personal assets, and significant unpaid withholding tax can lead to bankruptcy proceedings, director travel restrictions, and personal criminal records.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company, Sham Substance and Treaty Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the AG without employees, premises, Swiss board meetings, or real business activity; using the Swiss entity solely as an invoicing or IP-holding conduit to obtain the 5% reduced DTA dividend rate or the 100% Swiss participation exemption; back-to-back licensing with no Swiss value creation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authorities may deny treaty benefits under the beneficial-ownership and principal-purpose provisions of the Switzerland-China DTA, reallocate profits to the foreign shareholder under Swiss substance-over-form and anti-abuse doctrine, refuse the participation relief, and impose evasion penalties of up to three times the associated tax; elimination of the AG's status as a tax-resident company may result in its income being taxed in the hands of the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false substance declarations or tax-residence attestations face civil liability for the refused refunds and penalties, criminal proceedings for aiding tax evasion, and potential personal seizure of assets; repeated abuse may trigger a cantonal prohibition on acting as director and a Swiss entry or return ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Money Laundering and Payment-Rails Compliance (AMLA / Embargo)
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using Stripe/Paddle to accept payments originating from sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions, knowingly processing funds derived from fraudulent remote-access or IoT intrusion services, or failing to implement basic customer due diligence on resellers when the company's software is deployed for unlawful surveillance or unauthorised access.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Swiss Anti-Money Laundering Act (GwG), a company acting as a professional payment provider without the required SRO membership or FINMA authorisation may face fines of up to CHF 500,000 and revocation of authorisations; under Art. 305bis SCC, money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of up to three years; violations of Swiss embargoes and sanctions under the Embargo Act and SECO directives carry fines up to CHF 500,000 plus confiscation and debarment from public procurement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly or through gross negligence allow the platform to process illicit payments are criminally liable under Art. 29 VStrR and Art. 305ter SCC for inadequate financial due diligence; personal fines, travel bans and asset freezes may be imposed, and the corporate veil may be disregarded for civil restitution to victims of the illegal access.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Payroll and Social Security Liability Exposure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to enrol Swiss employees and directors with the compensation fund (AHV/AVS), under-deduction of OASI/DI/EO payroll contributions, non-registration for Swiss VAT on taxable Swiss SaaS turnover above the threshold, or deliberate misclassification of employees as independent contractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Swiss social security institutions will assess unpaid contributions with interest and surcharges of up to 5% of the missed amount; VAT shortfalls are subject to penalties of up to three times the evaded tax under Art. 70 MWSTG, plus default interest; deliberate VAT fraud triggers criminal proceedings with imprisonment up to three years; the employer can be barred from benefiting from payment facilitation providers if compliance flags arise.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Under Art. 52 DBG and the analogous provisions of the Swiss tax and social security statutes, directors are personally liable where culpable failure caused the non-payment; unpaid pension and social security debts are privileged claims in bankruptcy and directors face travel bans if they flee the country while debts are outstanding, as well as civil action by the compensation fund for the shortfall.
